title: `ia preview` and `ia author` admit checks structurally, as `ia validate` does
summary: @inventarch/cli: `ia preview` and `ia author` open their editor snapshot with structural check admission (plan amendment C21), as `ia validate` and `ia-distribution validate` open their session. A `@check` whose check.runs or check.implementation names one evaluator that is not built in is admitted there: an existing one is an owned record the edit forms can name, where the strict snapshot answered IA-CLI-EDIT-MISSING, and a new one previews clean and is written, where the strict snapshot counted IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN against the candidate and `ia author` refused it with IA-CLI-EDIT-UNCLEAN. A check naming no evaluator still counts against the candidate as IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN. Neither command lists or reads runtime evidence: the snapshot holds no record at runtime placement, and the base revision a preview prints is the evidence-free one every strict reader reports, while an evidence file for that authored revision exists. @inventarch/db: the ./editor subpath adds EditorOptions, which extends InputOptions with checks ('strict', the default, or 'structural', the values and default of OpenOptions.checks). EditorDatabase(root, options) and EditorSnapshot(input, changes, options) accept it, and a structural editor database's snapshot, its preview drafts, its candidates and every update or refresh admit structurally. A caller that passes no checks option keeps strict admission, as every other editor caller does. Limits: every other reader of the admitted graph stays strict, as the structural check admission note lists. Once `ia author` writes such a check, every strict reader counts it as an IA-COMP-CHECK-UNKNOWN error: ia host and ia project refuse the workspace (IA-CLI-CONFLICT, exit 3), ia capture still writes its snapshot with the finding recorded and exits 1, and ia validate's summary names the check.
